q-335588.name: Question 1
q-335588.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}=4x(1-0.25x)-3xy \\ {y}^{′}=-y+xy\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the Lotka-Volterra model with carrying capacity above, where $x=x(t)$ represents the prey and $y=y(t)$ represents the predators. The equilibria of the model are the following:

$(0,0),\,(${{field-1}}$,0),\,(${{field-2}}$,${{field-3}}$)$
q-335588.worked_solution:
The equilibrium (fixed) points of a system ${x}^{′}(t)=f(x,y)$ are the points for which $f(x,y)=0.$ So, we get the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}4x(1-0.25x)-3xy=0 \\ -y+xy=0\end{aligned}
$$

Factoring the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-y+xy & =0 \\ y(-1+x) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, $y=0$ or $x=1.$ We consider both cases separately.

- If $y=0,$ substituting it into the first equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}4x(1-0.25x)-3x(0) & =0 \\ 4x(0.25x-1) & =0 \\ x & =0,\,4.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the first two equilibria are $(0,0)$ and $(4,0).$

- If $x=1,$ substituting it into the first equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}4(1)(1-0.25(1))-3(1)y & =0 \\ 3-3y & =0 \\ y & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, another equilibrium is $(1,1).$

Therefore, the equilibria of the model are

$$
(0,0),\,(4,0),\,(1,1).
$$

q-335618.name: Question 3
q-335618.problem:
$$ \{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}=2x(1-x)-2xy \\ {y}^{′}=-2y+3xy\end{aligned} $$ Consider the Lotka-Volterra model with carrying capacity above, where $x=x(t)$ represents the prey and $y=y(t)$ represents the predators. Select the correct options in the reasoning below.$\,$ Evaluating the Jacobian of the system at the equilibrium ${x}^{∗}=[0,\,0]^{T},$ we get
$J({x}^{∗})=\,\,$ {{field-1}} {{field-2}} $\,.$
{{field-3}} {{field-4}}
$\,$ The eigenvalues of the Jacobian matrix are {{field-5}}. $\,$ Therefore, the equilibrium at ${x}^{∗}$ is {{field-6}}{{field-7}}.
q-335618.worked_solution:
Let's denote ${f}_{1}(x,y)=2x(1-x)-2xy$ and ${f}_{2}(x,y)=-2y+3xy.$

Now, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x(1-x)-2xy)=2-4x-2y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x(1-x)-2xy)=-2x \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-2y+3xy)=3y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(-2y+3xy)=-2+3x\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the Jacobian matrix is

$$
J=[\begin{aligned}2-4x-2y & -2x \\ 3y & -2+3x\end{aligned}].
$$

Next, we evaluate the Jacobian at the equilibrium ${x}^{∗}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ to get

$$
J({x}^{∗})=[\begin{aligned}2-4(0)-2(0) & -2(0) \\ 3(0) & -2+3(0)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

The eigenvalues of the Jacobian matrix are ${\lambda }_{1}=2\text{ and }{\lambda }_{2}=-2.$ Since the eigenvalues are real with opposite signs, our equilibrium is $\text{an unstable}$ $\text{saddle}.$

q-335670.worked_solution:
Let's denote ${f}_{1}(x,y)=5x(1-2x)-xy$ and ${f}_{2}(x,y)=-2y+3xy.$

Now, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(5x(1-2x)-xy)=5-20x-y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(5x(1-2x)-xy)=-x \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-2y+3xy)=3y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(-2y+3xy)=-2+3x\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the Jacobian matrix is

$$
J=[\begin{aligned}5-20x-y & -x \\ 3y & -2+3x\end{aligned}].
$$

Next, we evaluate the Jacobian at the equilibrium ${x}^{∗}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ to get

$$
J({x}^{∗})=[\begin{aligned}5-20(0)-0 & -0 \\ 3(0) & -2+3(0)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

The eigenvalues of the Jacobian matrix are ${\lambda }_{1}=5\text{ and }{\lambda }_{2}=-2.$ Since the eigenvalues are real with opposite signs, our equilibrium is $\text{an unstable}$ $\text{saddle}.$
